title: When the Static Sings
premise: When gravity fails for nine seconds across the solar system, Rosalind Thackeray discovers the anomaly originated from the seed vault he has guarded for five years — a dormant alien lattice buried beneath it that responds to human neural patterns. The fleet's two factions, the Wakers who want to revive their half of cryosleep and the Keepers who hoard power, each need him to activate it, because whoever wakes first will inherit a habitable Earth. As the truce expires, Rosalind learns the lattice demands a bonded mind as its price, and that his long-dead partner's consciousness is trapped inside it. In the end, he refuses both factions, merges with the lattice himself to hold Earth in trust, and broadcasts the waking codes to all sleepers equally — dying into the static so no faction can claim the future alone.
about_author: Tamsin Okonkwo is a former radio astronomer from Lagos who left academia after a decade of listening to signals no one else believed were real. She writes slow-burning science fiction about people who keep things running while history happens elsewhere.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A routine cargo haul from the seed vault to Ceres station is shattered when gravity flickers system-wide; his ship tumbles, his cargo scatters, and every instrument records the same impossible waveform. The chapter establishes his loneliness, his loyalty to the vault's mission, and ends with him realizing the signal's origin point is directly beneath him.

chapters.title: The Lattice Beneath the Seeds
chapters.summary: Rosalind descends into the vault's sealed sublevels and finds a crystalline structure threaded through the bedrock, older than the vault itself, humming with the same nine-second pattern. When he touches it, he hears a voice he recognizes: his partner Idris, dead five years. Emotional beat: grief weaponized — hope arriving dressed as a trap.

chapters.title: Two Flags on One Frequency
chapters.summary: Waker envoy Captain Adeyemi and Keeper liaison Voss arrive simultaneously at the vault, each claiming jurisdiction under the truce. Rosalind hides what he heard but realizes both sides already know something woke. POV alternates between Rosalind and Adeyemi's logs. Beat: the reader sees how easily loyalty becomes currency when survival is rationed.

chapters.title: What the Sleepers Dreamed
chapters.summary: Idris's voice teaches Rosalind to interface with the lattice through dreams, revealing it reads intention, not commands — and that it has been evaluating humanity for decades. He also learns the cryo-fleet's manifest was falsified: half the sleepers are already dead, their pods kept warm as leverage. Beat: betrayal reframes the entire war.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Waking
chapters.summary: Voss offers Rosalind command of the vault and priority waking for his own family's pod if he aligns with the Keepers; Adeyemi offers truth and nothing else. Rosalind runs the numbers: the lattice can wake everyone, but only if someone bonds with it permanently. POV: Rosalind, with interludes from Idris inside the lattice. Beat: temptation wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: Truce Expiry
chapters.summary: The truce timer hits zero and both fleets move on the vault. Rosalind triggers the lattice defensively, freezing all weapons in orbit for another nine seconds — proving he controls it and making himself the most valuable hostage alive. Beat: power arrives uninvited, and he feels its first corruption in how good it feels to be needed.

chapters.title: Idris, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Inside the lattice, Rosalind finds Idris's consciousness fragmenting; the lattice kept him as a template, not a soul. Idris begs Rosalind not to trade his life for a memory. Meanwhile Voss discovers the dead-sleeper cover-up and threatens to broadcast it, fracturing her own faction. POV splits three ways. Beat: love versus truth, fully priced.

chapters.title: The Bonding Protocol
chapters.summary: Adeyemi defects from the Waker hardliners to help Rosalind reach the lattice core before Voss's strike team breaches the vault. The bonding sequence begins — neural dissolution mapped in visceral detail — while Idris's remnant fights to buy time. Beat: sacrifice chosen freely, which is the only kind that counts.

chapters.title: Static Becomes Song
chapters.summary: Climax. Rosalind merges with the lattice as fleets converge; from inside, he halts every weapon, opens every cryo-pod's code simultaneously, and lets the dead be mourned publicly. Voss, confronted with the truth she threatened to reveal, chooses to stand down rather than rule ashes. Beat: the system-wide gravity flicker returns — this time as the lattice singing every mind awake.

chapters.title: Caretaker
chapters.summary: Resolution, one year later. Humanity wakes on a healing Earth governed by no one, with Adeyemi keeping an honest archive and Voss serving out penance rebuilding the fleet. In the vault, seeds sprout around a humming crystal where a new voice sometimes answers visitors — patient, plural, and unmistakably Rosalind's. Final beat: loyalty outlives the self that held it.
